Property.Name: DisplayName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

Property.Name: AdjustedThruputQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The total quantity that has been thruput from this container. Adjusted Thruput Qty = CurrentThruputQty - ThruputAdjustmentQty

Property.Name: AdjustedThruputQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The total quantity that has been thruput from this container. Adjusted Thruput Qty2 = CurrentThruputQty2 - ThruputAdjustmentQty2

Property.Name: BillOfProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: BinSize
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Size of the Packaging Unit

Property.Name: BOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product.

Property.Name: Carrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: ChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A count of the direct children of this container.

Property.Name: ComponentContainers
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a list of containers that have been issued to this container.

Property.Name: ConsumingOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Consuming Order is a String field

Property.Name: ContainerComments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Comments or notes specific to this Container.

Property.Name: CrossRefs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a full list of History Cross References as opposed to CurrentCrossRefs, which is a subset of this list, whose history entries apply to this container.

Property.Name: CurrentCrossRefs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a list of history cross references whose history entries apply to this container.

Property.Name: CurrentHoldCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Count of the number of containers on hold in the container structure starting at this container and tracing down through of all its descendants. If this container itself is currently directly on hold, and 2 of its children are also on hold, the CurrentHoldCount would equal 3.

Property.Name: CurrentStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Current Status CDO contains the current location information for one or more containers. Each container will have a reference to a single Current Status CDO.

Property.Name: CurrentStepPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of times the Container has passed through this Step.

Property.Name: CurrentThruputChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the number of child containers that have been processed at the current step.

Property.Name: CurrentThruputQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the quantity of the material that has been processed at the current step.

Property.Name: CurrentThruputQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the quantity2 of the material that has been processed at the current step.

Property.Name: CurrentThruputUnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the number of Units that have been processed at this step.

Property.Name: Customer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If specified, this field is a reference to the Customer to which this Container belongs. This is used to provide WIP Status by Customer inquiries.

Property.Name: DataPointCollections
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A DataPointCollection contains a list of DataPointCollectionGroup objects. A DataPointCollection can be attached to any object and allows the User entering the data to dynamically add extra samples of defined DataPoints and also dynamically define and collect new DataPoints.

Property.Name: DateCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date Code

Property.Name: Description
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: Direction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies the direction the material is mounted on a machine - 0, 90, 180, etc

Property.Name: DueDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time by which this Container is scheduled to complete. This is used with projected completion time for performance reporting

Property.Name: DueDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time by which this Container is scheduled to complete. This is used with projected completion time for performance reporting

Property.Name: ExpirationDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date/time after which the Container is no longer considered first quality.

Property.Name: ExpirationDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Factory where this Container is currently located.

Property.Name: FactoryStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time when this container arrived at or was created in the current factory.

Property.Name: FactoryStartDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time when this container arrived at or was created in the current factory.

Property.Name: FactoryStartQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity for this Container when it arrived at or was created in the current factory.

Property.Name: FactoryStartQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity for this Container when it arrived at or was created in the current factory.

Property.Name: FactoryStartUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The UOM for the container when it arrived at or was created in the current factory.

Property.Name: FactoryStartUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The UOM for the container when it arrived at or was created in the current factory.

Property.Name: ForwardProcessing
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates that the container has moved forward past optional workflow steps

Property.Name: HoldMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Hold Message to be displayed if specified

Property.Name: HoldReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container can be placed on "Hold" for the purpose of preventing additional work (for that Container). If specified, this field is the reason code identifying why the Container is Held.

Property.Name: InProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field determines whether or not work has been started at the current step. This is used to differentiate between Containers that are being processed and those that are In-Queue. This value is set to false when a Container first "arrives" at a Step. There are several transactions (Move-in, collect data, etc.) that change this value to True.

Property.Name: InQualityControl
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag set to improve reporting and prevent shipping of affected product.

Property.Name: InQueueTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Time as a duration

Property.Name: InRework
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Whether the container is in Rework or not.

Property.Name: IsInProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Non persistent read only boolean to state that the container is currently in process.

Property.Name: IsOnHold
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Non persistent boolean to state whether the container is on hold.

Property.Name: IssueConditions
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Issue Condition is used to control the issuance of components that are tracked as Containers using Issue Control - Issue Container (Bulk) or Issue Container (Serialized).

Property.Name: IssuedToContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The container to which this container was issued as a component.

Property.Name: LastActivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time for the last transaction for this specific Container. This is not changed when a transaction is executed against the parent.

Property.Name: LastActivityDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time for the last transaction for this Container. This is not changed when a transaction is executed against the parent.

Property.Name: LastCompletionDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time that thruput was last recorded for this Container.

Property.Name: LastCompletionDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time that thruput was last recorded for this Container.

Property.Name: LastMoveDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time of the last step change or when work was started.

Property.Name: LastMoveDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time of the last step change or when work was started.

Property.Name: LeadFree
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NotSet, No, Yes

Property.Name: Level
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the tracking level for this container. This value is set when the Container is created and may not (should not?) be changed.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current physical location of this Container, if specified. The Factory has a configuration option which is used to determine if this is a required field.

Property.Name: LoopPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of times the container has moved and remained at the same step

Property.Name: MaterialList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents, the list of components required to complete the production of a container. The necessary quantities or proportions of the item are specified as are the appropriate units of measure and other attributes. Note that this field is a calculated field, typically is configured to check the ContainerMaterialList, then the MfgOrder MaterialList, the the BOM MaterialList; using the first MaterialList it finds.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Manufacturing Order to which this Container belongs. This is used to provide WIP Status by Manufacturing Order and as interface information for integration with an ERP system.

Property.Name: MfgPartNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Manufacturer Part number

Property.Name: Name
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name for this Container. Container level definition is used to determine if this value must be unique.

Property.Name: NextOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default next Operation for this container. This is determined using the current Status and evaluating the workflow model.

Property.Name: NextStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default next Step for this container. This is determined using the current Status and evaluating the workflow model.

Property.Name: NextTxn
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default next transaction for this Container. This is determined using the current Status and evaluating the Workflow Model

Property.Name: NickName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Alternate name for the Container

Property.Name: NonconformanceReports
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The NonconformanceReport is used to track Non-conforming material. It includes attributes for analytic data (Failure, Cause, Resolution, etc) as well as attributes to identify the material that failed (Container and component information).

Property.Name: OnHoldDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the container was put on hold when the CurrentHoldCount = 0. In other words, then date/time the container changed from a status of "not held" to "held".

Property.Name: OpenEvents
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Open events for container which are loaded dynamically

Property.Name: OpenNonconformanceReports
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Open NonconformanceReport list is loaded dynamically

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current Operation for this Container.

Property.Name: OriginalContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Container from which this Container originated. This will only be different from the current Container Id if this Container was created by a Split-type transaction.

Property.Name: OriginalFactory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Factory where this Container originated (Create or Split-to transaction).

Property.Name: OriginalQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Original quantity for this Container.

Property.Name: OriginalQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Original quantity for this Container.

Property.Name: OriginalStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time when this Container originated (Start or Split-to transaction).

Property.Name: OriginalStartDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time when this Container originated (Start or Split-to transaction).

Property.Name: OriginalUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The UOM for the container when it was originally created.

Property.Name: OriginalUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The UOM for the container when it was originally created.

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Owner (Code) for this Container. Owners are used to select and group Containers for reporting. WIP Messages can also be defined for an Owner Code, which means they apply to all Containers with that Owner.

Property.Name: Parent
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Parent Container, if any. This value will only be set if this Container has been associated with another Container (as its child). This can be done using the Start or Associate transaction.

Property.Name: PlannedProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the product (a specific revision) this Container is intended to produce.

Property.Name: PlannedQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity of Product (planned) this Container is intended to produce.

Property.Name: PlannedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: PlannedStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date when processing is scheduled to commence on this container.

Property.Name: PlannedStartDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date when processing is scheduled to commence on this container.

Property.Name: PrevOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Operation where the Container was most recently Moved

Property.Name: PrevSpec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Spec where the Container was most recently Moved

Property.Name: PrevWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: PrevWorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Previous SpecStep where the Container was Moved

Property.Name: Priority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Priority codes are User Defined codes used to provide a descriptive and a relative priority for a Container.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current product for this Container (this will always be a specific revision of a Product).

Property.Name: ProductionComplete
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag to mark the container as having completed production.

Property.Name: ProjectedDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Projected date and time when this Container will be complete. This value is calculated using the current quantity and workflow step and then iterating though the workflow using standard setup times, run rates and yields.

Property.Name: ProjectedDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Projected date and time when this Container will be complete. This value is calculated using the current quantity and workflow step and then iterating though the workflow using standard setup times, run rates and yields.

Property.Name: ProjectedQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Projected quantity when this Container completes. This value is calculated using the current quantity and workflow step and then iterating though the workflow using standard setup times, run rates and yields.

Property.Name: ProjectedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current quantity of material in the container.

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current quantity of material in the container.

Property.Name: QtyToBeProcessed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The total quantity that has yet to be processed from this container. Qty Remained For Processing = Qty - AdjustedThruputQty

Property.Name: QtyToBeProcessed2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The total quantity that has yet to be processed from this container. Qty Remained For Processing2 = Qty2 - AdjustedThruputQty2

Property.Name: RelativePriority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a numeric value that is used to sequence Containers for Dispatching (What do I work on next?). There are multiple algorithms that can be resolved to a single numeric value. This (use of a field) is a simple approach to dividing the algorithm from the Dispatching.

Property.Name: RemainingProcessTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Remaining Process Time value, used for RPT calculation.

Property.Name: Reprocessing
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Is this Container currently being reprocessed (Moved) at its previous Step?

Property.Name: RequestDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If specified, this field represents the date and time when the Customer would like to receive (the material represented by) this Container.

Property.Name: RequestDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If specified, this field represents the date and time when the Customer would like to receive (the material represented by) this Container.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Resource where this Container is currently being processed (or will be processed). By default, this is the Resource that will receive the Production (throughput) credit for processing this Container.
Move-in sets this field to the Resource that is (will be) doing the work. By default that is the Resource that is used for Completion and Move-out transactions.
The Resource specified here is the Resource that will show this Container in its list of current Containers.

Property.Name: RollupUnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The effective UnitCount that would be used to roll up the UniCounts on all the ancestor Containers

Property.Name: SalesOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is an optional field available for relating this Container to a specific Sales Order. This provides a mechanism for allocating (and re-allocating) WIP to customer orders.

Property.Name: SamplingLot
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to associate a group of containers for sampling. For example, an Incoming inspection lot where multiple containers are from the same lot of material, received at different times but has one AQL Sampling.

Property.Name: SamplingPassed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the result of Sampling for the container. If All Sample Test Passed for this container then SamplingPassed = True. If one Sampling Test Failed then SamplingPassed = False

Property.Name: SamplingRequired
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if sampling is required for this container. Sampling is required when value is true

Property.Name: ShapeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: SPCChartSaveOptionsEnum
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: 1.Always - Automatically creates and saves the chart image 2.On Failure - Only creates and saves the SPC chart image if a SPC failure resulted 3.Never - never generates a SPC Chart image

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current Spec of the Container.

Property.Name: SplitFrom
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Container from which this Container was created. This will only have a value if this Container was created by a Split-type transaction.

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the Start Reason (Code) for this Container. Start reasons are primarily used for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history). WIP Messages can also be defined for an Start Reason Code, which means they apply to all Containers with that Start Reason.

Property.Name: Status
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: Supplier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supplier name

Property.Name: SupplyFromName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supply Form Name

Property.Name: SupplyFromType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: ThisContainerLost
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates whether or not this container was indicated as lost (completely scrapped) by the ChangeQty transaction.

Property.Name: ThruputAdjustmentChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Count of children adjusted during Thruput.

Property.Name: ThruputAdjustmentQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: ThruputAdjustmentQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: ThruputAdjustmentUnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Count of units adjusted in Thruput.

Property.Name: UnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of Unit containers in this container.

Property.Name: UOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unit of measure

Property.Name: UOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unit of measure

Property.Name: VendorItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Vendor Items are the products the vendor sells. This item is specified in the Product where, for purchased products, one can relate the product to a list of sources where the product can be purchased. In addition, when issuing components to a container, one can specify the VendorItem used to fulfill the component requirement.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the current top level workflow for this Container.

Property.Name: WorkflowNavigator
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Navigate through a workflow, including subworkflows and rework information.

Property.Name: WorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the list of subworkflow steps that lead to the current spec step.

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current workflow step for this Container. Step is used to access a Spec for processing information and Paths for movement processing.

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

NavigationProperty.Name: AttachDocumentDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The details used to display the attached documents.

NavigationProperty.Name: Attributes
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A user attribute is used to record a single value, identified by a unique name and attached to an object as a list. This is different from a set of single fields because the attributes can be different based on many factors, such as product or factory.

NavigationProperty.Name: ChildContainers
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: List of all the Child Containers for this Container. This list will only be set if this Container has been associated with other Containers (as their Parent). This can be done using the Start or Associate transaction.

NavigationProperty.Name: ContainerMaterialList
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents a the list of components that is required to produce the container. The necessary quantities or proportions of each component are specified as are the appropriate units of measure and other attributes. This particular type of material list item is used on Containers, and was created so that Container component lists could be stored in a separate table from BOM or MfgOrder component lists.

NavigationProperty.Name: ContainerSampleData
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to record all sampling plan data for a container. The sampling plan data is stored in this objects in order to keep updates from a user to the SamplingPlan from changing once the container has started its sampling plan tested. This is also used to provide selection data for the user on the Collect Sampling transaction. The next container will pick up the new changes.

NavigationProperty.Name: Detail
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A detail object of the container CDO. The intent is that the end user extends the detail object instead of extending the container object itself.

NavigationProperty.Name: GateStatus
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: List of all Gate Status’ with which this Container is currently associated. This list gets updated when the Container enters or leaves a Gate. The entries within the list or updated (as applicable) when transaction are performed within a Gate.

NavigationProperty.Name: SpecStatus
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A Spec Status is used to manage the status of a Container for the duration of processing against its current Spec. This includes tracking completed Transactions (when applicable), and determining if it is valid for the Container to Move to another Step (processing is completed for the current Spec).

NavigationProperty.Name: WIPMsgDefMgr
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A WIPMsgDef CDO that contains WIP messages and logic to process for a container

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Count of Associated Packages

Property.Name: Base
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the base for this revision. The RevisionBase holds information common to all revisions of an object, plus information on which revision is the revision of record.

Property.Name: Description
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: ECO
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Engineering Change Order

Property.Name: FilterTags
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: FilterTags comma seperated list

Property.Name: IconId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifier for the icon associated with this Base Entity

Property.Name: InstanceLocked
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if the instance is locked by Change Management

Property.Name: IsFrozen
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if changes are allowed to this instance

Property.Name: IsRevOfRcd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if this instance is the current Revision of Record (by comparing ID to BaseEntity.RevisionOfRecord)

Property.Name: ModelingInstanceLocks
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: List of Change Packages where modeling instance is assigned

Property.Name: Name
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name for this instance

Property.Name: Notes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Notations and comments associated with this object.

Property.Name: Revision
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Revision (unique within the context of the base entity)

Property.Name: Status
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Determines the current status (Active, In-Active) of this instance. Valid values and their meanings are:
1 = Active 2 = Inactive
Note there are no validations (rules enforced) concerning active vs. inactive revisions.

Property.Name: WhereUsed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A list of this type is returned by the Where-used functionality of a maintenance service. An instance of this CDO will specify one of the objects using the object to change. The fields in this CDO are used to populate a tree view displayed while maintaining a modeling object.

NavigationProperty.Name: ChangeHistory
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Every modeling entity includes a Change Status. It is used to record the current Change (Maintenance) Status (i.e., maintenance is currently in progress for a specific Product Definition) and to track who made the last change and when. This should be extendible to a complete history over time.

The text for completion messages is stored in labels and can be customized per user if necessary.

Property.Name: EffectivityDate

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user who will get credit for the work performed. Not necessarily the user who is logging the transaction.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The factory where the work was performed. The container must exist in the factory specified here. Usually this field is not input by the user.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Password

Property.Name: SmartBarcode

Property.Name: SmartScanParseError
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Smart parsing from CLF will not throw an error. If any error does occur, a message will be output here. The calling CLF can decide what to do with it.

Property.Name: SmartScanRule

Property.Name: StrSplitResult

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the service was performed. If left blank InSite uses the database system clock to determine the transaction date.

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

NavigationProperty.Name: LiveRelayInfo
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: LiveRelayInfo. Contains all of the information to perform the Remote Service and Response. It is primarily used for communication between InSite sites: for instance when containers are shipped.

NavigationProperty.Name: SmartScanParseResults

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Tracks the Workstation(s) assigned to the Container.

Property.Name: CurrentStepPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of tracked times the Container has entered the Current Workflow Step.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Describes a factory to the application. Factories are defined within an Enterprise. Users are authorized to perform work (Transactions) within Factories. Products include a list of the Factories where they can be manufactured. A Factory contains zero or more Locations.

Property.Name: InitialRecipeList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the RecipeList used to start the MaterialContainer

Property.Name: InProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field determines whether or not work has been started at the current step. This is used to differentiate between Containers that are being processed and those that are In-Queue. This value is set to false when a Container first "arrives" at a Step. There are several transactions (Move-in, collect data, etc.) that change this value to True.

Property.Name: InQueueTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Amount of time container was waiting in queue

Property.Name: InRework
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Whether the container is in rework.

Property.Name: LastCompletedTask
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The last Task completed for the Task.

Property.Name: LastMoveDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time of the last step change or when work was started.

Property.Name: LastMoveDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time of the last step change or when work was started.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: LoopPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of times the container has moved and remained at the same step

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ReworkTotalCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Total number of times the container is reworked.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The spec specified in the step when the container enterred the operation.

Property.Name: TimersCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Integer

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: WorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a list of workflow steps in the workflows leading to the current step.

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

NavigationProperty.Name: ContainerCompletedTasks
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: The list of completed Tasks for the Container at its current step. The list is cleared when the Container leaves the step.

NavigationProperty.Name: ReworkStatus
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: ReworkStatus stack to keep track of multiple levels of rework.

NavigationProperty.Name: StepPassCounts
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a CurrentStatus SubEntity which is used to keep track of the number of times a Step is passed during the life time of a container.

Property.Name: AdditionalESigReqs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Contains the list of Additional ESignature Requirements that should be collected in a single transaction.

Property.Name: Application
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique identifier for the Application which created this transaction.

Property.Name: AttachDocumentHistories
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Keeps track of all the Documents attached and detached form NDOs, RDOs and Containers

Property.Name: AttributeDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The history of the start transaction detailing the Attribute Values that were added to the container on the Start.

Property.Name: Authorizations
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the person or people who authorized the values in this transaction to be recorded out-of-spec (if applicable).

Property.Name: BaseTxnType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: As delivered, most transactions will return the current transaction type. Some transactions are grouped however. MoveOut, MoveStd, MoveNonStd, Rework are all MoveTxns for example.

Property.Name: Batch
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Batch represents the materials that are the final result of the production process. The Batch contains or references all the information about the specific Containers that represent the tracked materials that are the final result of the process.

Property.Name: BinningIncluded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This transaction recorded Binning information.

Property.Name: BizRuleHistory

Property.Name: BonusIncluded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This transaction recorded Bonus data.

Property.Name: CalendarShift
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Manufacturing shift based on the TxnTime and WorkSchedule from the WorkCenter where the work was perfomed.

Property.Name: Carrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: Client
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique identifier for the workstation (Client) where the transaction was recorded.

Property.Name: CompoundTxnType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Transaction type of outer compound transaction if any

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Container associated with the transaction, if applicable.

Property.Name: DefectIncluded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This transaction recorded Defect data.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indentifies the person who performed the work.

Property.Name: ESigDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The detail history for the collection of ESignatures.

Property.Name: ESigRequirement
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Contains the list of signatures that were collected for the transaction.

Property.Name: ESigSummaries
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The summary history for the collection of ESignatures.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Factory where the work was perfomed.

Property.Name: HistoryId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique identifier associated with all Containers participating in this transaction.

Property.Name: IconId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique identifier for an Icon. Most instances of data have an associated Icon. This is the ID used to uniquely identify the Icon within the Icon library.

Property.Name: Implicit
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The transaction that generated this CDO had an implicit effect on the container specified by this mainline CDO.

Property.Name: InRework
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates if the container is in Rework. Used primarily for reports that show the extra effort/cost that was incurred due to rework conditions.

Property.Name: LabelDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: History Detail information for every label printed. One History Detail record will be created for every printed label.

Property.Name: LabelSummaries
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: History Summary information for every label printed. One History Summary record will be created for every printed label.

Property.Name: LocalReworkIncluded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This transaction recorded Local Rework information.

Property.Name: Login
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user logged in when the transaction was recorded.

Property.Name: LossIncluded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: General purpose True/False field value.

Property.Name: MassUpdates
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: List of executed SQL statements that are associated with this transaction.

Property.Name: MfgDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Factories often have shift schedules that result in a shift starting work on one date and ending on another date; where 12 midnight is in the middle of the shift. For these factories, it is normal to have a concept of "Manufacturing Date" that enables any particular shift to fall entirely on one particular manufacturing day. A factory with shifts that start at 7am, 3pm, and 11pm will normally have a "Manufacturing Date" that begins on 11pm of the previous clock date, and ends at 11pm of the current clock date.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Operation where the transaction took place.

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Product Definition describes a product to the application. This may be a Product to be manufactured, raw materials, finished, etc. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: QualityESigConfirmed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The flag indicates is the Txn confirmed by the Quality Electronic Signature

Property.Name: RemainingProcessTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Remaining Process Time value, used for RPT calculation.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource where the transaction took place.

Property.Name: ResourceAvailability
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Defines the current availability status for a Resource. Valid values and their meanings are:
1 = Up (Available) 2 = Down (Not available)

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

Property.Name: ResourceStatusReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Resource Status Reason Code is used to provide an added level of detail describing the reason for the current status of a Resource. For example, the current status may be REPAIR. A Status Reason Code can be used to provide additional details such as the type of repair that is being performed. This detail is included in the transaction history, which makes it available for Analysis Reporting.

Property.Name: ReversalStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
The status of this record in relation to Transaction Reversal. Values are: 1 = "Active" A non-reversed transaction has been executed. The ReversalStatus is initially set to this value for all committed transactions.
2 = "Deleted" A reversal transaction has been executed. Once a transaction has been reversed, it's original HistoryMainline record is preserved, but the "ReversalStatus" is changed to deleted.
3 = "Reversal" A reversal transaction has been executed. A new HistoryMainline record is created for each "deleted" transaction. The data of the new HistoryMainline is based on the original transaction data, but the ReversalStatus is set to "Reversal". The User and DateTime stamp reflect the details of the ContainerTxnRev service. New copies of the corresponding history summaries and history details are created for the reversed transaction. Fields (such as the quantity fields in the history detail) are negated that have the flag "Txn Reversal-Compensate" checked on the Properties advanced tab. The "deleted" record will have a positive quantity, and the "reversal" record will have a negative quantity, and when summed (ie:reporting), the total will be zero.

Property.Name: Server
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique identifier of the Server that processed the transaction.

Property.Name: ShiftName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Typically applies to manufacturing companies that have areas staffed for a long enough during a day that workers do not all start and end their day at the same time. Shift is a mechanism for grouping production information based on management responsibilities for workers that start and leave at a particular time. For example, the "Day" shift might work from 6am to 6pm, and the "Night" shift would work from 6pm to 6am.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: Status
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Determines the current status (Active, In-Active) of this instance. Valid values and their meanings are:
1 = Active 2 = Inactive

Property.Name: StepPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of times the Container has passed through this Step.

Property.Name: SystemDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time that this transaction was recorded.

Property.Name: SystemDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time that this transaction was recorded.

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the work represented by this transaction was performed.

Property.Name: TxnDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the work represented by this transaction was performed.

Property.Name: TxnServiceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name of the service and is stored in History Mainline for shop floor services

Property.Name: TxnServiceSequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the sequence of services being executed within a transaction. In a compound transaction or container transactions that calls other container transactions, multiple services may be called. Since all of them are having the same TxnId and TxnDate, this field is then used to indicate the sequence of services being executed.

Property.Name: TxnType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Transaction type. Returns "MyMove" as opposed to "Move".

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the person who recorded the transaction.

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Workflow Step where the transaction took place (or started, i.e. <From> step is written for transactions like <Move>).

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: Counted
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: For sample data collected of this type, the user must enter the number of samples taken during transaction execution. The user enters a count for each data point (reject type). All data point values are summed to arrive at the total number of rejects. Counted Sample Test never have data point limits configured.

Property.Name: Measured
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: For sample data collected of this type, each data point represents a single sample. Data points are configured with limits. Data point limit failures are recorded as Rejects (one possible Reject per data point). All data point limit violations are summed to arrive at the total number of rejects. Measured data collections always have at least one limit configured for each data point.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ServiceTypeId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: CDO Definition Id of Default Service

Property.Name: ServiceTypeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the CDO Definition of Default Service

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: WorkCenterIconId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default identifier for the Icon to display with an instance of a Work Center

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The default Workstation for the Employee.

Property.Name: DurationPerUnit
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the amount of time needed to process a single unit. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: FastCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is a calculated value that denotes the time required processing a standard size batch of material using this Spec, assuming fast queue time. This is used to determine, for example, how quickly a job can be expedited through the Factory.
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: IsFrozen
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if changes are allowed to this instance (or any of its revisions)

Property.Name: NormalCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is a calculated value that denotes the time required processing a standard size batch of material using this Spec, assuming normal queue time.
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: RunRateOption
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This option determines if run rate is specified as hours per unit or units per hour or time per batch. The values and their meanings are: 1 = Hours per unit (RunRateTime) 2 = Unites per hour (RunRateQuantity) 3 = Time Per Batch (RunRate Time)

Property.Name: SetupTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the time required for a Setup at this Operation. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: StdBatchSize
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the standard size of a batch of material processed using this Spec. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: TimePerBatch
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specified the time needed to process a single Batch.

Property.Name: UnitsPerHour
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the number of units processed in an hour. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: UnscheduledTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Process time that is not contained in the UPH,HPU or Batch Time entries.

Property.Name: Yield
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies the standard yield expected for processing with this Spec. This value is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: Document
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Most Modeling entities include a reference to a document. Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. Each instance of a document (CDO) includes an identifier for the external document (i.e., a file name or a URL) and a reference to the program used for presenting the document.
Documents are also used to define recipe files for downloading to machines. In this case, presenting the Document means presenting it (downloading it) to a machine.

Property.Name: HoldReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: WIP Messages can be used to apply a hold to WIP (Containers). This is accomplished by associating a Hold Reason with the WIP Message definition. When the message is processed, the container is put on hold.

Property.Name: LITCListCDO
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This CDO always resides in one of several lists that originate from the maintenance CDO. This field contains the OID of the CDO that contains the list that contains this CDO.

Property.Name: LITCListField
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This CDO always resides in one of several lists that originate from the maintenance CDO. This field contains the ID of the field that contains the list that contains this CDO. It is used in conjuction with LITCListCDO to uniquely identify the field.

Property.Name: MsgAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Action Definition is a mechanism for providing all of the information required to invoke an action (i.e., launch a CLF) as part of a transaction. Examples of where this might be used include:
- Trigger corrective action through a Cell Control application - Activating a WIP Message in order to stop a given process - Sending a notification message to a specific Notification Target

Property.Name: NotificationTargets

An e-mail message is a typical example. The Notification Target describes the mechanism for delivering the message (e-mail, page, fax, system alert, etc.) and any additional details that are required for a particular delivery mechanism.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if changes are allowed to this instance (or any of its revisions)

Property.Name: NewOwner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: ReworkReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Process Rework Code is used to provide a list of reasons for Process Rework. The code is associated with a Container when it enters a rework loop. It is then associated with all throughput transactions generated by the container while it is in the rework loop. This provides, for example, a means of differentiating between first pass and rework throughput in reporting.

Property.Name: ToContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

Property.Name: ToContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ToContainerOption
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
If the Transaction Type is Combine then this option is used to determine specifics of the Combine:
1 = Create the To-Container (using auto-naming if configured) 2 = Combine to a Specific Container (and create it if it does not exist)

Property.Name: TxnType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Type of transaction to use:

Property.Name: CalendarDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Factories often have shift schedules that result in a shift starting work on one date and ending on another date; where 12 midnight is in the middle of the shift. For these factories, it is normal to have a concept of "Manufacturing Date" that enables any particular shift to fall entirely on one particular manufacturing day. A factory with shifts that start at 7am, 3pm, and 11pm will normally have a "Manufacturing Date" that begins on 11pm of the previous clock date, and ends at 11pm of the current clock date.

Property.Name: FiscalMonth
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Accounting information that describes how to group manufacturing dates into accounting periods (typically Year, Quarter, Month, and Week).

Property.Name: FiscalQuarter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Accounting information that describes how to group manufacturing dates into accounting periods (typically Year, Quarter, Month, and Week)

Property.Name: FiscalWeek
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Accounting information that describes how to group manufacturing dates into accounting periods (typically Year, Quarter, Month, and Week).

Property.Name: FiscalYear
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Accounting information that describes how to group manufacturing dates into accounting periods (typically Year, Quarter, Month, and Week).

Property.Name: IsFrozen
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if changes are allowed to this instance (or any of its revisions)

Property.Name: Shift
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Typically applies to manufacturing companies that have areas staffed for a long enough during a day that workers do not all start and end their day at the same time. Shift is a mechanism for grouping production information based on management responsibilities for workers that start and leave at a particular time. For example, the "Day" shift might work from 6am to 6pm, and the "Night" shift would work from 6pm to 6am.

Property.Name: ShiftEnd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The end time of the shift.

Property.Name: ShiftStart
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The start time of the shift.

Property.Name: Team
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An alternate means of grouping production information to "shift". For example, "day" and "night" shifts that are schedule to work on Monday-Thursday might be assigned to team "Red", while day and night shifts that work Friday-Sunday would be assigned to team "Blues".

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Is Rework

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Named Object Group that represents a group of Resources.

Property.Name: ReworkReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Process Rework Code is used to provide a list of reasons for Process Rework. The code is associated with a Container when it enters a rework loop. It is then associated with all throughput transactions generated by the container while it is in the rework loop. This provides, for example, a means of differentiating between first pass and rework throughput in reporting.

Property.Name: SubClassification
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to subclassify QualityObjects

Property.Name: TimerAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration for TimerActionEnum 1 = EndTxnNotExecute 2 = EndTxnExecute

Property.Name: ToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: ToStepName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ToWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: ToWorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sub-Workflow Step is used to reference a Workflow from another Workfow. This allows, for example, the re-use of Workflows for Rework processing.

Property.Name: ToWorkflowStack-Expanded
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expanded property for working with Key functionality.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Priority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Priority of the KPI

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: RecipeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Recipe Name

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource Type, a Resource categorization. Resources with the same Resource Type may share the same Resources Status Model.

Property.Name: RouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: TargetValue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Target Value

Property.Name: UOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: ThruputReportingLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
