A Work Center contains zero or more Operations. The primary use of a Work Center is dispatching and scheduling work. Resources (machines) are associated with a Work Center.

NavigationProperty.Name: SchedulingDetail
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations:
Operation Scheduling Details
An Operation uses an instance of Scheduling Details to define scheduling information at the most generic level. Each value in the scheduling details can be overridden by a Spec (referencing the Operation). The calculation for cycle time is:
( ( (RunTime + SetupTime) / Utilitzation ) + MoveTime + [Fast/Normal]QueueTime ) [/ HoursPerDay]
The hierarchy built-in to the application model is that Scheduling details specified at the Operation level can be overridden by a Spec. In turn the values in the Spec can be overridden by each Step that references that Spec. It is also assumed that Scheduling Details will be overridden at the Product or Product Family level. Further, the assumption is that this will be for a few Steps (if any) and that adding user-defined fields to the Product or Product Family definition (and then updating the field overrides) will address it.

NavigationProperty.Name: WIPMsgDefMgr
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Attached to an instance of a modeling entity, this contains the messages that apply to the entity. When asked to supply its WIP Messages, a modeling entity will ask its WIPMsgDefMgr to supply a list of WIP Messages that have been filtered to include only the messages that apply to the current circumstances (step, operation and label). The WIPMsgDefMgr will check the AllKey WIPMsgKey (which contains a message that applies to all steps) if specified, and run through the entries in the OperationKeys and LabelKeys lists and filter each message found.

A Setup Definition describes the work required, materials required, and estimates how long it will take to setup for a specific task. A typical use of a Setup Definition is to describe what it will take to prepare a machine for processing a batch or multiple batches of material. A Setup can reference an external document and/or an InstructionSet to describe the setup work required.
Each Setup can also include a reference to a Recipe file for downloading to a machine. Recipe files are stored as Documents. The associated Document Viewer is the program to launch for downloading (the recipe) to a machine.

Property.Name: ResourceGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An ObjectGroup is used to provide a list of objects, such as a list of Resources, Products or User Codes of a particular type. These lists are typically used for validation and selection. For example, an Operation includes a reference to a LossCodeGroup. The entries in this list define the valid Loss (reason) Codes for work performed while a Container is at that Operation.
An instance of an ObjectGroup includes a list of specific objects and a list of ObjectGroups. This list of objects for any given ObjectGroup is restricted to a specific type (or any of its derived types). Likewise, the list of ObjectGroup s within the ObjectGroup is restricted to the same type (or any of its derived types).

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Customer refers to a company that receives goods and services. Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Factory often represent a physical or logical plant. A Factory can be any division, department, section, or group that is separated for accounting and reporting purposes. A Factory often represents a physical manufacturing building.

Property.Name: LocalContainerStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status of the Container on the Local Site that is being set when it is sent to the ShipmentDestination. Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: RemoteContainerStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status of the Container on the Remote Site that is being set when it is received at the ShipmentDestination. Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: RemoteSite
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Destination (Remote) Site for the RemoteService.

Property.Name: Level
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.Name: MMAPIConnection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material Management API Connection

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: ProductType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Product Type Codes are used to differentiate between types of product such as WIP, Raw Material, Finished Goods, etc.

Property.Name: SRCAPIConnection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: SRC API Connection

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: LocalSite
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A site is defined as an independent InSite entity within a manufacturing organization. While a factory is a physical facilities concept, a site is a self contained IT structure based on a single transaction processing database, along with the associated InSite servers that provide the capability to generate transactions in the database. A factory could have one or more sites; and a site could run one or more factories.

Property.Name: LocationIconId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default identifier for the Icon to display with an instance of a Location

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ServiceTypeId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: CDO Definition Id of Default Service

Property.Name: ServiceTypeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the CDO Definition of Default Service

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: UserProfile
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Session information for an employee

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: FastCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is a calculated value that denotes the time required processing a standard size batch of material using this Spec, assuming fast queue time. This is used to determine, for example, how quickly a job can be expedited through the Factory.
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if changes are allowed to this instance (or any of its revisions)

Property.Name: NormalCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is a calculated value that denotes the time required processing a standard size batch of material using this Spec, assuming normal queue time.
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: RunRateOption
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This option determines if run rate is specified as hours per unit or units per hour or time per batch. The values and their meanings are: 1 = Hours per unit (RunRateTime) 2 = Unites per hour (RunRateQuantity) 3 = Time Per Batch (RunRate Time)

Property.Name: SetupTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the time required for a Setup at this Operation. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: StdBatchSize
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the standard size of a batch of material processed using this Spec. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: TimePerBatch
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specified the time needed to process a single Batch.

Property.Name: UnitsPerHour
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This value specifies the number of units processed in an hour. This is used in cycle time and Cost Accounting calculations.

Property.Name: UnscheduledTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Process time that is not contained in the UPH,HPU or Batch Time entries.

Property.Name: Yield

Property.Name: MsgAction

An Action Definition is a mechanism for providing all of the information required to invoke an action (i.e., launch a CLF) as part of a transaction. Examples of where this might be used include:
- Trigger corrective action through a Cell Control application - Activating a WIP Message in order to stop a given process - Sending a notification message to a specific Notification Target

Property.Name: MsgText

Property.Name: NotificationTargets
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Notification Target is used to define the recipient of a message that originates during the processing of a transaction. An e-mail message is a typical example. The Notification Target describes the mechanism for delivering the message (e-mail, page, fax, system alert, etc.) and any additional details that are required for a particular delivery mechanism.

Property.Name: SendNotification

1 = Active 2 = Inactive

Property.Name: CalendarDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Factories often have shift schedules that result in a shift starting work on one date and ending on another date; where 12 midnight is in the middle of the shift. For these factories, it is normal to have a concept of "Manufacturing Date" that enables any particular shift to fall entirely on one particular manufacturing day. A factory with shifts that start at 7am, 3pm, and 11pm will normally have a "Manufacturing Date" that begins on 11pm of the previous clock date, and ends at 11pm of the current clock date.

Property.Name: Shift
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Typically applies to manufacturing companies that have areas staffed for a long enough during a day that workers do not all start and end their day at the same time. Shift is a mechanism for grouping production information based on management responsibilities for workers that start and leave at a particular time. For example, the "Day" shift might work from 6am to 6pm, and the "Night" shift would work from 6pm to 6am.

Property.Name: ShiftEnd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The end time of the shift.

Property.Name: ShiftStart
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The start time of the shift.

Property.Name: Team
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An alternate means of grouping production information to "shift". For example, "day" and "night" shifts that are schedule to work on Monday-Thursday might be assigned to team "Red", while day and night shifts that work Friday-Sunday would be assigned to team "Blues".

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Named Object Group that represents a group of Resources.

Property.Name: ReworkReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Process Rework Code is used to provide a list of reasons for Process Rework. The code is associated with a Container when it enters a rework loop. It is then associated with all throughput transactions generated by the container while it is in the rework loop. This provides, for example, a means of differentiating between first pass and rework throughput in reporting.

Property.Name: SubClassification
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to subclassify QualityObjects

Property.Name: TimerAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration for TimerActionEnum 1 = EndTxnNotExecute 2 = EndTxnExecute

Property.Name: ToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: ToStepName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ToWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: ToWorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sub-Workflow Step is used to reference a Workflow from another Workfow. This allows, for example, the re-use of Workflows for Rework processing.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Priority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Priority of the KPI

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: RecipeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Recipe Name

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource Type, a Resource categorization. Resources with the same Resource Type may share the same Resources Status Model.

Property.Name: RouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: TargetValue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Target Value

Property.Name: UOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: Name
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of unique instance of resource

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: i) Sub-class of Resource. ii) No maintenance service. iii) Provides common fields to its sub-classes.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Y Location of the resource

Property.Name: EscalationRecipients
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: WebDrillDownMenuDefinition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Menu definitions are used to create custom menus on the customers own user interface. Menu Definitions consist of a collection of predefined commands. Through the use of Menu Definitions the needs of different groups of employees can be met in a factory. For example, employees in an operation might be responsible for moving containers and collecting container parametric data, while employees in another operation might be responsible for starting and grouping containers. In both cases, they should see a different menu and therefore they would have a different Menu Definition.

Property.Name: FHMResolvedAreaResources
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Used for the "Factory Hiararchy Model". Get all resources for a factory with a factory level set to "Area". The tree of child resources can then be traversed.
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: LastRPTWeekly

Property.Name: LocalSite
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A site is defined as an independent InSite entity within a manufacturing organization. While a factory is a physical facilities concept, a site is a self contained IT structure based on a single transaction processing database, along with the associated InSite servers that provide the capability to generate transactions in the database. A factory could have one or more sites; and a site could run one or more factories.

NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations:
Used for the "Factory Hiararchy Model". Get all resources for a factory with a factory level set. This provides a 'flat' version of the resource hiararchy.
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

NavigationProperty.Name: WIPMsgDefMgr
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Attached to an instance of a modeling entity, this contains the messages that apply to the entity. When asked to supply its WIP Messages, a modeling entity will ask its WIPMsgDefMgr to supply a list of WIP Messages that have been filtered to include only the messages that apply to the current circumstances (step, operation and label). The WIPMsgDefMgr will check the AllKey WIPMsgKey (which contains a message that applies to all steps) if specified, and run through the entries in the OperationKeys and LabelKeys lists and filter each message found.

Property.Name: CurrentSetup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Setup Definition describes the work required, materials required, and estimates how long it will take to setup for a specific task. A typical use of a Setup Definition is to describe what it will take to prepare a machine for processing a batch or multiple batches of material. A Setup can reference an external document and/or an InstructionSet to describe the setup work required.
Each Setup can also include a reference to a Recipe file for downloading to a machine. Recipe files are stored as Documents. The associated Document Viewer is the program to launch for downloading (the recipe) to a machine.

Property.Name: FHMResolvedChildResources
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Used with the factory hiararchy model. Get all children of this resource with a factory level set.
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An ObjectGroup is used to provide a list of objects, such as a list of Resources, Products or User Codes of a particular type. These lists are typically used for validation and selection. For example, an Operation includes a reference to a LossCodeGroup. The entries in this list define the valid Loss (reason) Codes for work performed while a Container is at that Operation.
An instance of an ObjectGroup includes a list of specific objects and a list of ObjectGroups. This list of objects for any given ObjectGroup is restricted to a specific type (or any of its derived types). Likewise, the list of ObjectGroup s within the ObjectGroup is restricted to the same type (or any of its derived types).

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status of the Container on the Local Site that is being set when it is sent to the ShipmentDestination. Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: RemoteContainerStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status of the Container on the Remote Site that is being set when it is received at the ShipmentDestination. Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: Resources
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: EmployeeRecipients
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Level
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.Name: MMAPIConnection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material Management API Connection

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: ProductType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Product Type Codes are used to differentiate between types of product such as WIP, Raw Material, Finished Goods, etc.

Property.Name: SRCAPIConnection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: SRC API Connection

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

NavigationProperty.Name: ToStages
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: This is an optional sub-entity list that can be used to provide alternate next stage to move the resource to. If a Detail has no ToStages configured, the next stage will follow the StageSequence in the JobModel's Details. If specified, the ToStageSelector for each ToStage will be evaluated until a success (i.e. true) is detected and the next stage will be set to it. The user can select ToStage without ToStageSelectors. If all ToStageSelectors return false, the next stage will follow the StageSequence in the JobModel’s Details.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.

Property.Name: ForwardCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is the sum of all NormalCycleTime from this step through the end of the Workflow (following defaults Paths from this Step forward).
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: ForwardYield
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Standard (cumulative) yield from this step through the end of the Workflow (following defaults Paths from this Step forward).
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. Each instance of a document (CDO) includes an identifier for the external document (i.e., a file name or a URL) and a reference to the program used for presenting the document.

Property.Name: ERPRoute
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.

You can define and apply an alternative scheduling route that can be used to identify steps for scheduling integration. Instances of scheduling routes will take precedent over ERP route. If no Scheduling Routes are configured or detected by the application, the ERP Route will be used by default.

Property.Name: TotalCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is the sum of all through the Workflow (following defaults Paths).
Note: The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: TotalYield
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Standard (cumulative) yield through the Workflow (following defaults Paths).
Note: The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: MaxQueueTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value determines the maximum length of time a Container can remain in an in-queue state at the Step that uses this Spec. The value for MaximumQueueTimeAction determines the action to take if the in-queue time exceeds this value.

Property.Name: MaxQueueTimeAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value is used to determine the action to take when a Service (transaction) is started for a Container that has been in-queue longer than the allowable queue time (MaxQueueTime).
The values for this option are: 0 = No action 1 = Warning to Operator 2 = Warning to Operator requiring a password to continue 3 = Place container on Hold 4 = Do not allow transaction to continue
These values and their associated actions are intended to match the values and actions for field validations.
This action applies to any service that changes a Container from an In-Queue to an In-Process state.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Operation where this work is to be performed. This value is used as the default Operation when a new Step is created (using this Spec). If specified, this must be a valid (defined) Operation

Property.Name: Optional
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies whether the step is considered optional and can be skipped

Property.Name: PostProductionAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
What to do when production completed for an Mfg Order with a configured post-production procedure
1 - EnableProcedure 2 - RequireProcedure

Property.Name: RecipeFile
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Most Modeling entities include a reference to a document. Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. Each instance of a document (CDO) includes an identifier for the external document (i.e., a file name or a URL) and a reference to the program used for presenting the document.
Documents are also used to define recipe files for downloading to machines. In this case, presenting the Document means presenting it (downloading it) to a machine.

Property.Name: ActionSource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to filter Actions.

Property.Name: AdditionalESigReqs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Contains the list of ESignature Requirements that should be collected in a single transaction.

Property.Name: AlertMsgList
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A string list used holds the additional messages of a transaction

Property.Name: AlertMsgListDelimiter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A string field used to define the delimiter string to separate the additional messages

Property.Name: CalledByTransactionTask
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If this transaction is being performed as part of an e-procedure, this is the TransactionTask where it was specified.

Property.Name: Comments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Free-form text notes the user can provide when performing a service.

Property.Name: CompletionMsg
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: When the service is executed, this field will be filled out by the system with a message in the terminology of the user and language that describes the successful completion of the service, or describes the error condition if there was an error. The text for completion messages is stored in labels and can be customized per user if necessary.

Property.Name: DataCollectionDef
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Data Collection Definition used to define the parametric data fields to collect and place in ParametricData. If there is only one reference to this specific service in the Spec TransactionMap, InSite will fill in this field automatically. If a service exists multiple times in the TransactionMap, the user will need to input which data collection definition they are using. For instance, the CollectData service might be entered twice on the TransactionMap, once with parameters recorded every hour, and once with parameters recorded every ten minutes. When the user is performing the ColllectData, the user would then need to specify which kind of data collection they are performing in this field.

Property.Name: DispatchItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Facilitates the configuration of dispatching rules for MfgOrders and Containers on Shopfloor services. Only one entry per dispatch item type will be allowed to be configured.

Property.Name: DispatchRule
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field represents the existence of an order dispatch type within the dispatch rule, used in the enforcement of the Dispatch Rule.

Property.Name: EffectivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This date/time is used in a comparison against EffectiveDates in modeling entities to help determine if the object should be considered for processing. This value is always specified as GMT time.

Property.Name: EmailGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Fields that can be used to identify the EmailGroup to send an email to. Some transactions allow the user to set the EmailGroup to send to such as LotHold and LotRelease.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user who will get credit for the work performed. Not necessarily the user who is logging the transaction.

Property.Name: EnableRPT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag to determine whether the service will trigger the RPT calculation.

Property.Name: EnforceDispatch
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Boolean flag to override dispatch enforcement.

Property.Name: ESigRequirement
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The signature requirement for the spec/service combination. Only one should be defined for the combination.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The factory where the work was performed. The container must exist in the factory specified here. Usually this field is not input by the user.

Property.Name: HasDataCollection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns true if the associated service has a data collection assigned, false otherwise.

Property.Name: HasDPCollection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag allows the client to determine if the data collection type is of type DataPointCollection.

Property.Name: HasUserDataCollection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag allows the client to determine the type of data collection to process, UserDataCollection or ParametricDataCollection.

Property.Name: IsExternalAppTxnExecution
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The flag indicates whether a transaction was initiated by an external application, such as through a REST API call. This field is crucial for managing data broadcasts, like controlling a SignalR broadcast. By default, the flag is set to false, allowing normal broadcasting of data. However, when the flag is set to true, it serves as a control mechanism to prevent broadcasting the transaction data. This indicates that the transaction was executed externally, and therefore, should not be broadcast back.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows to alter standard processing of a Service in case it's executed as a Remote Service.

Property.Name: MfgCalendar
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Calendar that is used to translate the timestamp of when a transaction was performed into a specific manufacturing date and shift.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: ParametricDataControl
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: FileName - used for fields that specify files.

Property.Name: ParametricDataDefType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: CDO Definition Id

Property.Name: Password
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NT login password for the user performing the service, if "User" was entered. If "user" is not entered security is based on the InSite login.

Property.Name: PrintingResult
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Printing Result

Property.Name: PrintLabels
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: PrintQueue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Printers InSite can use to print labels.

Property.Name: ProcessActiveMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is a flag to enable the processing of active mfg orders, which will validate the resources' active mfg orders with the process container mfg orders.

Property.Name: ProcessEProcedures
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn off all the Electronic Procedures processing (validations and executions) in a single place.

Property.Name: ProcessESignatures
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies whether the Electronic Signatures should be validated and executed for the service. This is used to turn off the processing in the subservices when they are called from a compound (the Electronic Signature processing should take place in the compound).

Property.Name: ProcessMaintMgmt
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn off all the Maintenance Management processing (validations and executions) in a single place.

Property.Name: ProcessMasterRecipe
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn off all the Master Recipe processing (validations and executions) in a single place.

Property.Name: ProcessNCRs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn off all the NCRs processing (validations and executions) in a single place.

Property.Name: ProcessResourceStatusModel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag used to find and execute a StatusModelDetail with a PreconditionToAutoSet that returns true.

Property.Name: ProcessTrainingReqs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field provides a way to turn off all the Training Requirements processing (validations and executions) in a single place. Note that this is addition to the CheckTrainingReqs flag. The ProcessTrainingReqs will be used to turn off the feature globally, while the CheckTrainingReqs is used to control it at the individual service level.

Property.Name: RemainingProcessTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Remaining Process Time value, used for RPT calculation.

Property.Name: SampleQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Sample Qty

Property.Name: SamplingPlan
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to Define a sampling plan for a Product. The sample plan contains the details about the Sample Test for a Product such as where it is to be tested, AQL Level, and switching rules.

Property.Name: SamplingPlanDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The specific describes the details for a Sampling Plan's Sample Test.. For each Sample Test, the AQL Level, Inspection Level, Switching Rule, Spec, Vendor and Resoruce can be configured. Resolved from the Container

Property.Name: SpecFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is getting from Line Assignment and its meant to be used as a filter parameter for shopfloor queries.

Property.Name: ss_SPCRecipe
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A subclass of Document describes recipe.

Property.Name: TaskContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If this service is being performed as part of a e-procedure task, this is the container for which the e-procedure is being processed. This field is used top populate the ExecuteTaskService.Container field, and for ContainerTxns, this will be the same as the Container field. It is needed for the case where the service is not a Container Transaction, e.g. ResourceSetup.

Property.Name: TaskTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Time it took to perform the task

Property.Name: TrainingRequirements
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Definition of the training required before a user is allowed to perform a specific task

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the service was performed. If left blank InSite uses the database system clock to determine the transaction date.

Property.Name: TxnParentServiceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name of the parent service that calls a subservice.

Property.Name: TxnServiceSequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the sequence of services being executed within a transaction. In a compound transaction or container transactions that calls other container transactions, multiple services may be called. Since all of them are having the same TxnId and TxnDate, this field is then used to indicate the sequence of services being executed.

Property.Name: UseDispatch
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Configures a service to be enabled for using the dispatch functionality

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

Property.Name: WebPart
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ACEMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ACEMessage field contains the success or failure messages of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitFailure) On unhandled errors in these events, System automatically populates this field with the resolved error message.

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.Name: ServerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The server name that processed the transaction.

Property.Name: CurrentDay
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic String

Property.Name: CurrentMonth
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic String

Property.Name: Container

Property.Name: ContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The ChargeToStep is the processing step where the problem occurred. This step will be tracked by the nonconformance report that is about to be created.

Property.Name: ChargeToWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: CreateDateBegin
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: CreateDateEnd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: IncludeClosedNCRs
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: NCRFailureCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the problem that occurred.

Property.Name: NonconformanceReport
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is added to provide custom defined selection values that support paging. If this field is submitted by the client, it is then added to the list of NonconformanceReports

Property.Name: NonconformanceReports
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The NonconformanceReport is used to track Non-conforming material. It includes attributes for analytic data (Failure, Cause, Resolution, etc) as well as attributes to identify the material that failed (Container and component information).

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Workcenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: MaintenanceClass

Property.Name: MaintenanceStatus

Property.Name: NoState
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource doesn't entered the warning period defined by the assigned Maintenance Requirment.

Property.Name: PastDue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource is past due for maintenance and is no longer available for use.

Property.Name: Qty2Used
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty2 processed by the Resource.

Property.Name: QtyUsed
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty processed by the Resource.

Property.Name: RemainingDays
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Days remaining in which a Resource is still available for processing.

Property.Name: RemainingQty2Percent
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Percentage of Qty2 remaining to be processed.

Property.Name: RemainingQtyPercent
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Percentage of Qty remaining to be processed.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

Property.Name: WithinTolerance
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource is due for maintenance but is with the tolerance period defined by the assigned Maintenance Requirment.

Property.Name: WithinWarning
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource has entered the warning period defined by the assigned Maintenance Requirment.

Property.Name: MfgOrderFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: OperationFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: ParentContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ProductFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: MfgOrderFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: ProcessTimerFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Process Timer

Property.Name: ProcessTimerTypeFilter

Property.Name: ProductFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ShowTimers
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Show Timers With <= Mins Remaining

Property.Name: SpecFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.
