Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: Attributes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A user attribute is used to record a single value, identified by a unique name and attached to an object as a list. This is different from a set of single fields because the attributes can be different based on many factors, such as product or factory.

Property.Name: BillOfProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: BinSize
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Size of the Packaging Unit

Property.Name: Carrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: ChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Child count of the top level container created.

Property.Name: ConsumingOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Consuming Order is a String field

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ContainerComments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Notes/Comments assinged to the container, as opposed to assigned to the transaction.

Property.Name: Customer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Customer container is assigned to at the time of the start.

Property.Name: DateCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date Code

Property.Name: Description
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: Direction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies the direction the material is mounted on a machine - 0, 90, 180, etc

Property.Name: DueDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date the container is scheduled to be finished processing.

Property.Name: DueDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: GMT translation of DueDate.

Property.Name: ExpirationDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date/time after which the Container is no longer considered first quality.

Property.Name: ExpirationDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic TimeStamp

Property.Name: ForwardProcessing
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates that the container has moved forward past optional workflow steps

Property.Name: HoldMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Hold Message to be displayed if specified

Property.Name: InQualityControl
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag set to improve reporting and prevent shipping of affected product.

Property.Name: InQueueTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Time as a duration

Property.Name: IssueConditions
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Issue Condition is used to control the issuance of components that are tracked as Containers using Issue Control - Issue Container (Bulk) or Issue Container (Serialized).

Property.Name: LeadFree
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NotSet, No, Yes

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the physical location of the Container when it was started.

Property.Name: LoopPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of times the container has moved and remained at the same step

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The manufacturing order the container was assigned to at the time of the start. Manufacturing orders are typically scheduling constructs managed by an ERP system.

Property.Name: MfgPartNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Manufacturer Part number

Property.Name: NickName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Alternate name for the Container

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The operation (logical or physical description of where work in the factory is to be performed) where the container was started.

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: PlannedProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Expected resulting product for this container after all processing is complete.

Property.Name: PlannedQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty expected to be available from this container after all processing is complete.

Property.Name: PlannedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty expected to be available from this container after all processing is complete.

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unit of measure for the first planned quantity.

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unit of measure for the second planned quantity.

Property.Name: PlannedStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date when processing is scheduled to commence on this container.

Property.Name: PlannedStartDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date when processing is scheduled to commence on this container.

Property.Name: Priority
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Processing priority defined for the container at the time of the start. Each Priority Code includes a description and a Relative Priority value. The Relative Priority value is used to sequence Containers for dispatching (independent of the Code name or description). .

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.

Property.Name: ProductionComplete
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag to mark the container as having completed production.

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity of the container at the time of the start.

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity of the container at the time of the start.

Property.Name: RequestDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Typically, the date the customer requested this container be shipped.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The machine or other resource the container is associated with at the time of the start.

Property.Name: SalesOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sales Order defines a quantity of product expected by a customer by a date. This equates to a line item on a typical (ERP) Sales Order. Containers are optionally assigned to a Sales Order (by specifying the Sales Order as an attribute). This provides the mechanism for relating WIP (Containers) to Customer Orders.

Property.Name: SamplingLot
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to associate a group of containers for sampling. For example, an Incoming inspection lot where multiple containers are from the same lot of material, received at different times but has one AQL Sampling.

Property.Name: SamplingRequired
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if sampling is required for this container. Sampling is required when value is true

Property.Name: ShapeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: SPCChartSaveOptionsEnum
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: 1.Always - Automatically creates and saves the chart image 2.On Failure - Only creates and saves the SPC chart image if a SPC failure resulted 3.Never - never generates a SPC Chart image

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Reason. Start reasons are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: Supplier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supplier name

Property.Name: SupplyFromName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supply Form Name

Property.Name: SupplyFromType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: UnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unit count of the top level container created.

Property.Name: VendorItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Vendor Items are the products the vendor sells. This item is specified in the Product where, for purchased products, one can relate the product to a list of sources where the product can be purchased. In addition, when issuing components to a container, one can specify the VendorItem used to fulfill the component requirement.

Property.Name: WorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The workflow stack that was used when the container was created, defining where the container was is relation to subworkflows inside a workflow.

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: ActiveMfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: AllowedProducts
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This list is used to determine if it is valid to run a particular Container on this Resource. To be valid, the current Product for the Container must be in the list. The list is built by retrieving all Product Options where To-Product matches the current Product (setup) for the Resource.

Property.Name: Availability
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines whether or not this Resource is currently available (UP) for production. The status and reason fields provide additional detail.

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Container assigned to the Resource for LineClearance processing.

Property.Name: InProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies whether the Resource is InProcess for LineClearance processing.

Property.Name: JobCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the number of jobs for the resource that have yet to complete or cancelled.

Property.Name: LastActivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time (including DST and TZ) of the last transaction for this Resource.

Property.Name: LastActivityDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time of the last transaction for this Resource.

Property.Name: LastProcessedContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The last container that was processed via a move or movein operation using this resource.

Property.Name: LastRouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.

Property.Name: LastStatusChangeDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time (including DST and TZ) of the last Move-in or Move-out transaction for a Container using this resource.

Property.Name: LastStatusChangeDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time of the last Move-in or Move-out transaction for a Container using this resource.

Property.Name: LastThruputDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field identifies the date and time (including DST and TZ) of the last completion transaction for this Resource.

Property.Name: LastThruputDateGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field identifies the date and time of the last completion transaction for this Resource.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Optionally specifies to the Manufacturing Order for which the associate Resource is setup. This is used on the Container Start transaction to assign a Manufacturing Order to a Container that is started as this Resource.

Property.Name: PartDecommissioned
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether the part has been decommissioned.

Property.Name: PartExpiryDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The expiry date for the part.

Property.Name: PartExpiryStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status for PartExpiryDate. Valid values: - NULL - PENDING - Has reached the warning duration. - PENDINGDONE - Has been verified. - PENDINGSENT - Email has been sent. - DUE - Has reached the expiry date,

Property.Name: PartLifetimeCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the lifetime count for the part.

Property.Name: PartLifetimeCount2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the secondary lifetime count for the part.

Property.Name: PartLifetimeStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status for PartLifetimeCount. Valid values: - NULL - PENDING - The count has reached the warning limit. - PENDINGDONE - The count has validated. - PENDINGSENT - Email has been sent for PENDING. - DUE - The count has reached the limit. - DUEDONE - The count has validated. - DUESENT - Email has been sent for DUE.

Property.Name: PartLifetimeStatus2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status for PartLifetimeCount2. Valid values: - NULL - PENDING - The count has reached the warning limit. - PENDINGDONE - The count has validated. - PENDINGSENT - Email has been sent for PENDING. - DUE - The count has reached the limit. - DUEDONE - The count has validated.

Property.Name: PartQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the number of pieces.

Property.Name: PartQtyInRequest
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Virtual field used to return the quantity of the part currently reserved in one or more requests.

Property.Name: PartQtyInUse
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Virtual field used to return the quantity of the Part that is currently in loaded in one or more resources.

Property.Name: PartReconditionCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the number of times the part has completed jobs of Recondition type.

Property.Name: PartRequestCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the number of part requests for the resource that have yet to complete or cancelled.

Property.Name: PartUsageCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the usage count for the part.

Property.Name: PartUsageCount2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Stores the secondary usage count for the part.

Property.Name: PartUsageStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status for PartUsageCount. Valid values: - NULL - PENDING - The count has reached the warning limit. - PENDINGDONE - The count has validated. - PENDINGSENT - Email has been sent for PENDING. - DUE - The count has reached the limit. - DUEDONE - The count has validated. - DUESENT - Email has been sent for DUE.

Property.Name: PartUsageStatus2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status for PartUsageCount2. Valid values: - NULL - PENDING - The count has reached the warning limit. - PENDINGDONE - The count has validated. - PENDINGSENT - Email has been sent for PENDING. - DUE - The count has reached the limit. - DUEDONE - The count has validated. - DUESENT - Email has been sent for DUE.

Property.Name: PhysicalLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents the physical location within a factory.

Property.Name: PhysicalPosition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents the positions within a PhysicalLocation.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the Product this Resource is currently setup to run. This is used in the validation logic when starting work for a Container at this Resource (re: Move-in). This is also used to assign a Product to a Container that is started as this Resource.

Property.Name: ResourceState
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Resource State definition: 1. NonScheduled 2. UnscheduleDown 3. ScheduleDown 4. Engineering 5. Productive 6. Standby

Property.Name: Run
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current Setup number. This value is used to identify all of the work that is performed using a specific Setup. The value is set (incremented) as part of the Resource Setup transaction. All Throughput and Movement transactions record this value in their history transactions.

Property.Name: TotalThruputQty

Property.Name: TotalThruputQty2

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ForwardCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is the sum of all NormalCycleTime from this step through the end of the Workflow (following defaults Paths from this Step forward).
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: ForwardYield
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Standard (cumulative) yield from this step through the end of the Workflow (following defaults Paths from this Step forward).
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.

Property.Name: SchedulingRouteStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A step in anScheduling Route , which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. Scheduling Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.

Property.Name: Sequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Relative sequence of this Step within the Workflow. This value is used to retrieve (via SQL) Steps in order.

Property.Name: StepType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Denotes whether this Step references a Step or a Workflow. The values are: 1 = Spec 2 = Workflow

Property.Name: ToSteps
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The list of steps reachable from this step using its paths.

Property.Name: WIPMsgLabel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifier for relating a WIP Message to one or more Steps. WIP Messages defined for all Modeling Entities except a Step or Operation can be qualified with a WIP Message Label. This allows the same message to be associated with multiple Steps.

Property.Name: Workflow

Property.Name: Ylocation

NavigationProperty.Name: Paths

NavigationProperty.Name: PathSelectors
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Paths selectors are used to select a Path based on the value(s) of specific data within a transaction. Each Path selector includes an expression to evaluate and a Path to select. The expression to evaluate identifies a field (see note 1) to evaluate and a comparison value. The comparison value can be a single value, a range (from-through values), or a list of values. Expressions are evaluated in a defined sequence. The first expression that evaluates to true determines the Path to select.

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: ListItemToChange
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: OID of a list item for which this CDO is acting as proxy. Defaults to the OID of this CDO.

Property.Name: ResolvedPermission
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: For display purposes this field describes the resolved access for this specific function. This is necessary for multiple reasons. For example, a User may have different, overridding permissions as the member of a group or the value entered may be "0" (not specified). Also, this field only updates at the time the maintenance is loaded. Changing the "Access" field will set this field to <null>.

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ContainerComments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Comments or notes specific to this Container - populated by CVE

Property.Name: ContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

Property.Name: ContainerLevelName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used for textual read-only display of the ContainerLevel

Property.Name: ContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name identifyer of the selected Container

Property.Name: CurrentThruputQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: CurrentThruputQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: DueDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time by which this Container is scheduled to complete. This is used with projected completion time for performance reporting

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Factory often represent a physical or logical plant. A Factory can be any division, department, section, or group that is separated for accounting and reporting purposes. A Factory often represents a physical manufacturing building.

Property.Name: HoldReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Associating a Hold Code with a Container prevents transactions from being performed for that Container. Hold Codes are User Defined to provide multiple descriptions (reasons) for Holds.

Property.Name: InProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field determines whether or not work has been started at the current step. This is used to differentiate between Containers that are being processed and those that are In-Queue.

Property.Name: InRework
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Whether the container is in Rework or not.

Property.Name: LastActivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time for the last transaction for this specific Container. This is not changed when a transaction is executed against the parent.

Property.Name: LastMoveDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time of the last step change or when work was started.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Manufacturing Order defines what to make and when it is needed. If they are used, a Manufacturing Order is typically the link between the MES and an ERP system. One Manufacturing Order relates to one or more Containers (WIP). The Manufacturing Order includes attributes that are used for starting Containers.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: NextOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Default next Operation for this container. This is determined using the current Status and evaluating the workflow model.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.

Property.Name: OriginalStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time when this Container originated (Start or Split-to transaction).

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

Property.Name: PlannedProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Product Definition describes a product to the application. This may be a Product to be manufactured, raw materials, finished, etc. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: PlannedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Quantity2 of Product (planned) this Container is intended to produce.

Property.Name: PlannedUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOM Container is intended to be a measure of

Property.Name: PlannedUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOM2 Container is intended to be a measure of

Property.Name: PriorityCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Priority Code is one method used to assign a processing priority to a Container. Each Priority Code includes a description and a Relative Priority value. The Relative Priority value is used to sequence Containers for dispatching (independent of the Code name or description). Priority Codes are only one of the algorithms used to determine a numeric value for Scheduling and Dispatching.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Product Definition describes a product to the application. This may be a Product to be manufactured, raw materials, finished, etc. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ProductDescription
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String representation of the current product description

Property.Name: ProductIsRevOfRcd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ProductIsRevOfRcd Determines if the current Product instance is the current Revision of Record (by comparing ID to BaseEntity.RevisionOfRecord)

Property.Name: ProductName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String representation of the current Product name

Property.Name: ProductRev
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String representation of the current Product revision

Property.Name: ProjectedDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Projected date and time when this Container will be complete. This value is calculated using the current quantity and workflow step and then iterating though the workflow using standard setup times, run rates and yields.

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Material quantity (individual)

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current quantity2 of material in the container.

Property.Name: QtyOperator
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: How to compare the qty filter against the current container qty 10 = Equal 20 = GreaterThan 30 = GreaterThanOrEqual 40 = LessThan 50 = LessThanOrEqual

Property.Name: RequestDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If specified, this field represents the date and time when the Customer would like to receive (the material represented by) this Container.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String representation of the current container resource

Property.Name: SalesOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sales Order defines a quantity of product expected by a customer by a date. This equates to a line item on a typical (ERP) Sales Order. Containers are optionally assigned to a Sales Order (by specifying the Sales Order as an attribute). This provides the mechanism for relating WIP (Containers) to Customer Orders.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: Specification
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
String representation of the current Spec. An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: SpecIsRevOfRcd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if this instance is the current Revision of Record (by comparing ID to BaseEntity.RevisionOfRecord)

Property.Name: SpecRevision
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String representation of the Spec revision

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: Status
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: StatusName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Status Name

Property.Name: Step
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: WorkflowIsRevOfRcd
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if this instance is the current Revision of Record (by comparing ID to BaseEntity.RevisionOfRecord)

Property.Name: WorkflowRev
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: String representation of the current workflow revision

Property.Name: Carrier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A carrier is a physical entity that holds material which is used in batch processing. Carriers are resources like: Vessels, Vats, drums, trays etc.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The factory (a physical or logical plant) where the container is located.

Property.Name: InProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field determines whether or not work has been started at the current step. This is used to differentiate between Containers that are being processed and those that are In-Queue. This value is set to false when a Container first "arrives" at a Step. There are several transactions (Move-in, collect data, etc.) that change this value to True.

Property.Name: InRework
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Whether the container is in rework.

Property.Name: Location
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The initial Resource on which this Container is started.

Property.Name: ReworkTotalCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Total number of times the container is reworked.

Property.Name: SpecStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines the spec step at which the container will be started.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference to the initial workflow on which the Container has been started

Property.Name: WorkflowStack
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a list of steps leading to the current workflow.

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference to the specific manufacturing step in a workflow for this Container start.

NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: StartDetails related to the Rework Status of a Container will go here

Property.Name: EndReworkStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the Step that triggers the end-of-rework logic. This means clearing the Rework Status and determining the appropriate "Next Step".

Property.Name: ReEntryStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies the "Next Step" after completion of Rework processing. If not specified then the default is the Rework-From Step.

Property.Name: ReworkReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the (user defined) reason code describing why this Container is being reworked. This value is used for inquiries and reporting (i.e., Rework by Reason Code Analysis).

EntityType.customAttribute:EventList: _DeleteMe; GetTrackableOwnerForAuditTrail; IsOKToUpdateAttachments; TxnRev_Add; TxnRev_Change; TxnRev_Delete; TxnRev_SaveUnreversedValues;

Property.Name: Availability
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The current availabilty of a resource.

Property.Name: PartDecommissioned
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating whether the part has been decommissioned.

Property.Name: PartExpiryDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The expiry date for part resource.

Property.Name: PartQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The part quantity for part resource.

Property.Name: PartQtyInRequest
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Virtual field used to return the quantity of the part currently reserved in one or more requests.

Property.Name: PartQtyInUse
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Virtual field used to return the quantity of the Part that is currently in loaded in one or more resources.

Property.Name: PhysicalLocation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents the physical location within a factory.

Property.Name: PhysicalPosition
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Represents the positions within a PhysicalLocation.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ProductName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ProductRev
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Revision (unique within the context of the base entity)

Property.Name: Reason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Resource Status Reason Code is used to provide an added level of detail describing the reason for the current status of a Resource. For example, the current status may be REPAIR. A Status Reason Code can be used to provide additional details such as the type of repair that is being performed. This detail is included in the transaction history, which makes it available for Analysis Reporting.

Property.Name: ReasonCodeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ResourceAvailability
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The integer value for the availability of the Resource.

Property.Name: Run
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current Setup number. This value is used to identify all of the work that is performed using a specific Setup. The value is set (incremented) as part of the Resource Setup transaction. All Throughput and Movement transactions record this value in their history transactions.

Property.Name: Setup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Setup is a configuration of a resource needed to process a certain type of material (typcially a particular product, or a container referencing a particular spec).. Normally the definition of a setup includes only items as hardware configurations, that take significant time to change, while a reciipe would include many other items such as process settings that may be changed instantly.
Standard Camstar-provided attributes of a setup include items such as the applicable set of documents describing the setup configuration, an estimate of time need to configure the setup, etc. Setups are often defined in InSite to help provide scheduling/dispatching information on which containers/orders may be processed without significant changeover time between the items.

Property.Name: SetupName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: SetupRev
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Revision (unique within the context of the base entity)

Property.Name: Status
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

Property.Name: StatusCodeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: TimeAtStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Integer

Property.Name: Tools
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns the tools current assigned to the Resource.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will be due for a maintenance event based on a recurring date requirement or a date requirement.

Property.Name: NextDateWarningGMT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will enter the warning state based on a recurring date requirement or a date requirement.

Property.Name: NextThruputQty2Due
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will be due for a maintenance event based on a Thruput requirement.

Property.Name: NextThruputQty2Limit

Property.Name: NextThruputQty2Warning
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will be enter the warning state based on a Thruput Requirement.

Property.Name: NextThruputQtyDue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will be due for a maintenance event based on a Thruput requirement.

Property.Name: NextThruputQtyLimit
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will be past due for a maintenance event based on a Thruput Requirement.

Property.Name: NextThruputQtyWarning
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifies when the Resource will enter the warning state based on a Thruput Requirement.

Property.Name: PastDue
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating if the Resource is past due for a maintenance defined in a Maintenance Requirement.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceName

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCode

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCodeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ResourceStatusCode name

Property.Name: ThruputQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Calculated ThruputQty based upon the ProductionStatus and MaintenanceStatus.

Property.Name: ThruputQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Calculated ThruputQty2 based upon the ProductionStatus and MaintenanceStatus.

Property.Name: UOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: UOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user code for unit of material.

Property.Name: UOM2Name
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOM2 name

Property.Name: UOMName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOM name

Property.Name: Warning
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag indicating if the Resource is in the Warning period of a Maintenance Requirement.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: ERPRoute
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.

This value determines the maximum length of time a Container can remain in an in-queue state at the Step that uses this Spec. The value for MaximumQueueTimeAction determines the action to take if the in-queue time exceeds this value.

Property.Name: MaxQueueTimeAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value is used to determine the action to take when a Service (transaction) is started for a Container that has been in-queue longer than the allowable queue time (MaxQueueTime).
The values for this option are: 0 = No action 1 = Warning to Operator 2 = Warning to Operator requiring a password to continue 3 = Place container on Hold 4 = Do not allow transaction to continue
These values and their associated actions are intended to match the values and actions for field validations.
This action applies to any service that changes a Container from an In-Queue to an In-Process state.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Operation where this work is to be performed. This value is used as the default Operation when a new Step is created (using this Spec). If specified, this must be a valid (defined) Operation

Property.Name: Optional
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies whether the step is considered optional and can be skipped

Property.Name: PostProductionAction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
What to do when production completed for an Mfg Order with a configured post-production procedure
1 - EnableProcedure 2 - RequireProcedure

Property.Name: RecipeFile
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Most Modeling entities include a reference to a document. Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. Each instance of a document (CDO) includes an identifier for the external document (i.e., a file name or a URL) and a reference to the program used for presenting the document.
Documents are also used to define recipe files for downloading to machines. In this case, presenting the Document means presenting it (downloading it) to a machine.

Property.Name: ERPRoute
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.

Property.Name: Gates
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: List of all the Gates for this workflow

Property.Name: RemainingProcessTimeEnabled
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag that enable RPT calculation.

Property.Name: SchedulingRoute
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Scheduling Route is a modeling object that allows configuration of specific scheduling routes without leveraging ERP routes. You can define and apply an alternative scheduling route that can be used to identify steps for scheduling integration. Instances of scheduling routes will take precedent over ERP route. If no Scheduling Routes are configured or detected by the application, the ERP Route will be used by default.

Property.Name: TotalCycleTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
This is the sum of all through the Workflow (following defaults Paths).
Note: The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: TotalYield
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Standard (cumulative) yield through the Workflow (following defaults Paths).
Note: The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ACEMessage field contains the success or failure messages of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitFailure) On unhandled errors in these events, System automatically populates this field with the resolved error message.

Property.Name: ACEStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure) Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.
Value Name Meaning 1 ACESuccess after commit event completed successfully 2 ACEFSuccess an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully 3 ACEFFail an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event > 99 <custom status> User specific status codes (Designer based)

Property.Name: Comments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Free-form text notes the user can provide when performing a service.

Property.Name: CompletionMsg
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: When the service is executed, this field will be filled out by the system with a message in the terminology of the user and language that describes the successful completion of the service, or describes the error condition if there was an error. The text for completion messages is stored in labels and can be customized per user if necessary.

Property.Name: EffectivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This date/time is used in a comparison against EffectiveDates in modeling entities to help determine if the object should be considered for processing. This value is always specified as GMT time.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The factory where the work was performed. The container must exist in the factory specified here. Usually this field is not input by the user.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows to alter standard processing of a Service in case it's executed as a Remote Service.

Property.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: Password
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NT login password for the user performing the service, if "User" was entered. If "user" is not entered security is based on the InSite login.

Property.Name: ServerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The server name that processed the transaction.

Property.Name: TxnDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date and time the service was performed. If left blank InSite uses the database system clock to determine the transaction date.

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user performing the data entry, used primarily for security validation. If not input, security is based on the login user.

Property.Name: DisplayName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

Property.Name: BaseToChange
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Names the revision base that will be modified by this maintenance service.

Property.Name: SyncRevision
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The revision of the object that we will try and resolve so it can be synced.

Property.Name: LabelToFind
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Identifier for relating a WIP Message to one or more Steps. WIP Messages defined for all Modeling Entities except a Step or Operation can be qualified with a WIP Message Label. This allows the same message to be associated with multiple Steps.

Property.Name: ObjectWithWIPMsg
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field refers to any object that has associated WIP Messages viz. UserCodeWithWM, Container, BOM etc. This field is basically used to reach to the WIP Message Manager, the object that has to be maintained by this service.

Property.Name: OperationToFind
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.

Property.Name: WIPMsgType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Type of WIP message: Operation Keys All Keys Label Keys
