If there is only one reference to this specific service in the Spec TransactionMap, InSite will fill in this field automatically. If a service exists multiple times in the TransactionMap, the user will need to input which data collection definition they are using. For instance, the CollectData service might be entered twice on the TransactionMap, once with parameters recorded every hour, and once with parameters recorded every ten minutes. When the user is performing the ColllectData, the user would then need to specify which kind of data collection they are performing in this field.

Property.Name: DispatchItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Facilitates the configuration of dispatching rules for MfgOrders and Containers on Shopfloor services. Only one entry per dispatch item type will be allowed to be configured.

Property.Name: DispatchRule
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field represents the existence of an order dispatch type within the dispatch rule, used in the enforcement of the Dispatch Rule.

Property.Name: EffectivityDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This date/time is used in a comparison against EffectiveDates in modeling entities to help determine if the object should be considered for processing. This value is always specified as GMT time.

Property.Name: EmailGroup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Fields that can be used to identify the EmailGroup to send an email to. Some transactions allow the user to set the EmailGroup to send to such as LotHold and LotRelease.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The user who will get credit for the work performed. Not necessarily the user who is logging the transaction.

Property.Name: EnableRPT
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag to determine whether the service will trigger the RPT calculation.

Property.Name: EnforceDispatch
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Boolean flag to override dispatch enforcement.

Property.Name: ESigRequirement
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The signature requirement for the spec/service combination. Only one should be defined for the combination.

Property.Name: Factory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The factory where the work was performed. The container must exist in the factory specified here. Usually this field is not input by the user.

Property.Name: HasDataCollection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Returns true if the associated service has a data collection assigned, false otherwise.

Property.Name: HasDPCollection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag allows the client to determine if the data collection type is of type DataPointCollection.

Property.Name: HasUserDataCollection
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag allows the client to determine the type of data collection to process, UserDataCollection or ParametricDataCollection.

Property.Name: IsExternalAppTxnExecution
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The flag indicates whether a transaction was initiated by an external application, such as through a REST API call. This field is crucial for managing data broadcasts, like controlling a SignalR broadcast. By default, the flag is set to false, allowing normal broadcasting of data. However, when the flag is set to true, it serves as a control mechanism to prevent broadcasting the transaction data. This indicates that the transaction was executed externally, and therefore, should not be broadcast back.

Property.Name: IsRemoteService
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Allows to alter standard processing of a Service in case it's executed as a Remote Service.

Property.Name: MfgCalendar
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Calendar that is used to translate the timestamp of when a transaction was performed into a specific manufacturing date and shift.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: ProcessEProcedures

Property.Name: TxnParentServiceName

Property.Name: Operation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ToStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: To Start Date

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: EmployeeFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: OperationFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. Property.Name: ResourceFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: Run
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current Setup number. This value is used to identify all of the work that is performed using a specific Setup. The value is set (incremented) as part of the Resource Setup transaction. All Throughput and Movement transactions record this value in their history transactions.

Property.Name: Setup
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Setup Definition describes the work required, materials required, and estimates how long it will take to setup for a specific task. A typical use of a Setup Definition is to describe what it will take to prepare a machine for processing a batch or multiple batches of material. A Setup can reference an external document and/or an InstructionSet to describe the setup work required.
Each Setup can also include a reference to a Recipe file for downloading to a machine. Recipe files are stored as Documents. The associated Document Viewer is the program to launch for downloading (the recipe) to a machine.

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: InspectionLevel

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: RequiredSamples
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Total samples required for the Container being inspected

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: SamplesTested
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Number of samples tested for the sample test.

Property.Name: SampleTest
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object used for defining instances of AQL SampleTest that describe the Data to collect and any events that should happen based on the collected data on the sample.

Property.Name: SamplingPlan
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to Define a sampling plan for a Product. The sample plan contains the details about the Sample Test for a Product such as where it is to be tested, AQL Level, and switching rules.

Property.Name: SamplingStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Sampling Status

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: TotalPassedSamples
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Number of Samples Passing the sample test for the transaction.

Property.Name: TotalRejects
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Total Rejects

Property.Name: TotalSamplesCompleted
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Total Samples Completed

Property.Name: Vendor
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A vendor is a provider of goods and services. An example of these goods and services are components and subassemblies used to manufacture products, products purchased for resale, non-production materials, services such as resource and building maintenance and so on.

Property.Name: VendorItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Vendor Items are the products the vendor sells. This item is specified in the Product where, for purchased products, one can relate the product to a list of sources where the product can be purchased. In addition, when issuing components to a container, one can specify the VendorItem used to fulfill the component requirement.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: WorkflowStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ChildContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.Name: ChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Number of child containers created/serialized using these details.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The upper control limit that was in effect at the time the out of control chart was generated

Property.Name: ViolationName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic String

An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.

Property.Name: Spec
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: HistoryEmployeeHistory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: InProcessFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration for the ContainerSearchFilter: -1 = Don't Filter 0 = Omit 1 = Include

Property.Name: InQualityControl
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: InQualityControl flag

Property.Name: InReworkFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration for the ContainerSearchFilter: -1 = Don't Filter 0 = Omit 1 = Include

Property.Name: IssuedComponentProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: IssuedContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: LAOperation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: LAResource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: LAWorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: LAWorkstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: OnHold
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: On Hold

Property.Name: OnHoldFilter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration for the ContainerSearchFilter: -1 = Don't Filter 0 = Omit 1 = Include

Property.Name: OpenNonConformances
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: OperationHistory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

Property.Name: ResetReworkStatus
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag to determine whether to reset the rework status.

Property.Name: ResourceHistory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: SpecHistory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

Property.Name: TxnFromDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Transaction From Timestamp

Property.Name: TxnToDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Transaction To Timestamp

Property.Name: WorkCenter
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.

The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: AttachAsROR
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates if the Doc to be attached will be ROR. This field is Visible when the user chooses Attach a new document that will not be reused or Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: AttachedDocument
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Reference to the newly created or resolved document attached, used for history summary / it is also used to retrieve selctin values for document in the web form, for when the user assigns an existing document

Property.Name: AttachedFileExtension
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Attached File Extension reference, used to store it to History

Property.Name: AttachedFileName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the File attached to the NDO, RDO or Container, used for History

Property.Name: AttachmentIsROR
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to determine if the existing document being attached is beng attached as the Revision of Record.

Property.Name: AttachmentType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Enumeration used to indicate what type of document attachment will be perfomed: 1 - Attach a new document that will not be reused (no Revision needed) 2 - Attach a new document that will be reused (Revision must be provided) 3 - Attach an existing document

Property.Name: AttributeSources
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The objects on which there are user attribute lists.

Property.Name: AutoNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: AutoNumberRule
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to define auto numbering rule.

Property.Name: BillOfProcess
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

Property.Name: BinSize
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Size of the Packaging Unit

Property.Name: BOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product.

Property.Name: ChildAutoNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Boolean

Property.Name: ChildCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of child Containers which are to be started for this Container.

Property.Name: ChildIndex
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Integer

Property.Name: ConsumingOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Consuming Order is a String field

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).

Property.Name: ContainerComment
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Comments or notes specific to this Container when started

Property.Name: ContainerInstance
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object used to get the information and ID of the selected Container instance and save it to history

Property.Name: ContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for the container

Property.Name: Customer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference to the Customer for whom this Container is being started

Property.Name: DateCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date Code

Property.Name: DefaultChildLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: ContainerLevel to be used for all the children created by this transaction for this container, unless overriden for a particular child.

Property.Name: DefaultChildQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty to be used for all the children created by this transaction for this container, unless overriden for a particular child.

Property.Name: DefaultChildQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Qty2 to be used for all the children created by this transaction for this container, unless overriden for a particular child.

Property.Name: DefaultChildUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOMl to be used for all the children created by this transaction for this container, unless overriden for a particular child.

Property.Name: DefaultChildUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: UOM2 to be used for all the children created by this transaction for this container, unless overriden for a particular child.

Property.Name: Description
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: Direction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Specifies the direction the material is mounted on a machine - 0, 90, 180, etc

Property.Name: DocumentDescription
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: DocumentName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Name of the Document being Attached. This field is Visible when the user chooses Attach a new document that will not be reused or Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: DocumentRevision
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Document Revision being Attached. This field is only visible when user chooses Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: DueDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Date and time by which this Container is scheduled to complete. This is used with projected completion time for performance reporting

Property.Name: ExpirationDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date/time after which the Container is no longer considered first quality.

Property.Name: FilePath
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: External identifier for a document (Path and file name, URL, etc.) Path for the document being uploaded. This field is visible when user chooses Attach a new document that will not be reused or Attach a new document that will be reused.

Property.Name: ForwardProcessing
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Indicates that the container has moved forward past optional workflow steps

Property.Name: HoldMessage
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Hold Message to be displayed if specified

Property.Name: Identifier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: External identifier for a document (Path and file name, URL, etc.)

Property.Name: InQualityControl
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This flag set to improve reporting and prevent shipping of affected product.

Property.Name: InQueueTime
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Time as a duration

Property.Name: IsContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Field used to determine if the object to attach the document to is a Container, this is used in the Web Page

Property.Name: IssueConditions
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Issue Condition is used to control the issuance of components that are tracked as Containers using Issue Control - Issue Container (Bulk) or Issue Container (Serialized).

Property.Name: LastSequence
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic Integer

Property.Name: LeadFree
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: NotSet, No, Yes

Property.Name: Level
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Container levels are used to define a type of container, and will typically denote the position of the container within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Lot, Wafer, and Die would be defined as container levels. Attributes of the Container Level are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

Property.Name: LoopPass
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of times the container has moved and remained at the same step

Property.Name: MfgOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Manufacturing Order defines what to make and when it is needed. If they are used, a Manufacturing Order is typically the link between the MES and an ERP system. One Manufacturing Order relates to one or more Containers (WIP). The Manufacturing Order includes attributes that are used for starting Containers.

Property.Name: MfgPartNumber
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Manufacturer Part number

Property.Name: NickName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Alternate name for the Container

Property.Name: NumberingRuleQryResult
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.Name: ObjectTypeId
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The CDO type Id for the object. List of all NDO, RDO, and Container objects.

Property.Name: OriginalContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) . A Container represents a grouping of other containers. The grouping allows a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. Containers are most often grouped together so a single workflow-oriented transaction such as a Move, MoveIn, or Transfer applies to the entire group of containers.

Property.Name: OriginalFactory
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Factory often represent a physical or logical plant. A Factory can be any division, department, section, or group that is separated for accounting and reporting purposes. A Factory often represents a physical manufacturing building.

Property.Name: Owner
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples",

Property.Name: ParentDetails
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference that provides a back pointer to the StartDetails CDO of the parent of this record.

Property.Name: PlannedProduct
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference to a Product CDO. The PlannedProduct is typically used by ERP systems when uploading a MPS ( Manufacturing Production Schedule) into InSite

Property.Name: PlannedQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The PlannedQty is typically used by ERP systems when uploading a MPS ( Manufacturing Production Schedule) into InSite. It is the Qty of units scheduled to be started

Property.Name: PlannedQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The PlannedQty2 is typically used by ERP systems when uploading a MPS ( Manufacturing Production Schedule) into InSite. It is the Qty2 of units scheduled to be started

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference. The PlannedQtyUOM is typically used by ERP systems when uploading a MPS ( Manufacturing Production Schedule) into InSite. It is the Unit of Measure of the units scheduled to be started

Property.Name: PlannedQtyUOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference. The PlannedQtyUOM2 is typically used by ERP systems when uploading a MPS ( Manufacturing Production Schedule) into InSite. It is the Unit of Measure 2 of the units scheduled to be started

Property.Name: PlannedStartDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The date when processing is scheduled to commence on this container.

Property.Name: PrevWorkflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: PriorityCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: An instance of a Priority Code is one method used to assign a processing priority to a Container. Each Priority Code includes a description and a Relative Priority value. The Relative Priority value is used to sequence Containers for dispatching (independent of the Code name or description). Priority Codes are only one of the algorithms used to determine a numeric value for Scheduling and Dispatching.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An instance of a Product Definition describes a product to the application. This may be a Product to be manufactured, raw materials, finished, etc. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ProductionComplete
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Flag to mark the container as having completed production.

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The initial quantity of material in the container.

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If multiple quantity types are being tracked ( such as pounds and packages ) then Qty2 represents the initial second tracking quantity

Property.Name: RequestDate
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If specified, this field represents the date and time when the Customer would like to receive (the material represented by) this Container.

Property.Name: SalesOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A Sales Order defines a quantity of product expected by a customer by a date. This equates to a line item on a typical (ERP) Sales Order. Containers are optionally assigned to a Sales Order (by specifying the Sales Order as an attribute). This provides the mechanism for relating WIP (Containers) to Customer Orders.

Property.Name: SamplingLot
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to associate a group of containers for sampling. For example, an Incoming inspection lot where multiple containers are from the same lot of material, received at different times but has one AQL Sampling.

Property.Name: SamplingRequired
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Determines if sampling is required for this container. Sampling is required when value is true

Property.Name: ShapeName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: SPCChartSaveOptionsEnum
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: 1.Always - Automatically creates and saves the chart image 2.On Failure - Only creates and saves the SPC chart image if a SPC failure resulted 3.Never - never generates a SPC Chart image

Property.Name: StartReason
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).

Property.Name: Status
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Property.Name: Supplier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supplier name

Property.Name: SupplyFromName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Supply Form Name

Property.Name: SupplyFromType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Description of this entity. Defaults to the name of this entity if not specified

Property.Name: UnitCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The number of Unit containers in this container.

Property.Name: UOM
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference to a user code which is used to express the quantity in the container. For example, Ea , Box, Carton, Lbs, Liters.

Property.Name: UOM2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Object reference to a user code which is used to express a secondary quantity in the container. For example, Ea , Box, Carton, Lbs, Liters. This is used when multiple UOMs are used simulataneously - like pounds and packages

Property.Name: UsingAttributes
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Conditions user attributes processing.

Property.Name: VendorItem
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Vendor Items are the products the vendor sells. This item is specified in the Product where, for purchased products, one can relate the product to a list of sources where the product can be purchased. In addition, when issuing components to a container, one can specify the VendorItem used to fulfill the component requirement.

Property.Name: Workstation
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

NavigationProperty.Name: AttachDocument
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: AttachDocument is a subclass of GenericTxn that is used to attach documents to any Container, NDO, or RDO object type. There are three ways to attach a document: 1. As a reusable document that can be attached to multiple instances of an object 2. As a document that will not be reused and is only attached to a single instance of an object 3. As a reference to an existing Document

NavigationProperty.Name: AttributeDetails
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: A user attribute is used to record a single value, identified by a unique name and attached to an object as a list. This is different from a set of single fields because the attributes can be different based on many factors, such as product or factory.

NavigationProperty.Name: ChildContainers
NavigationProperty.customAttribute:Annotations: Object Reference to a list of Container objects. This list comprises the child Containers of the current Container.

Property.Name: ThruputReportingLevel

Property.Name: UnitCount

Property.Name: AdjustThruput
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Defines whether the quantity being changed should be considered as already processed. If this flag is set to true, the ThruputAdjustmentQty in the container will be updated with the Qty from this CDO.

Property.Name: ChangeQtyType
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Type of ChangeQtyDetail : 1 = defect, 2 = loss, 3 = sell, 4 = adjust, 5 = bonus, 6 = buy

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Normally, a change in quantity is noted immediately. However, in some cases, a test performed at a step may show that an earlier step caused a change in quantity. This field allows the system to note the step that caused the quantity to change.

Property.Name: Comments
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Free-form text notes the user can provide regarding the specific container to which the change quantity is being performed.

Property.Name: Container
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The specific container against which the service is being performed. This container may be one of several containers being transacted against by a single Change Quanity transaction.

Property.Name: CountsAgainstProduction
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Has a value true for LossDetails and BonusDetails , false otherwise.

Property.Name: EnteredQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic String

Property.Name: EnteredQty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Generic String

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This field is used to track the amount of material lost for the specific container.

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: If the container is tracked using a second unit of measure, this field is used to track the amount of material lost for the specific container.

Property.Name: QtyMultiplier
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The product of this field and the Qty field will determine the values that will be used for the calculations. For positive changes (Buy, Bonus and Adjustments) the value will be 1. For negative changes (Losses and Sells) the value is a -1.

Property.Name: ReasonCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is the reason code attributed to the quantity being lost for the specific container. For version 1.3, reason codes are defined in the WorkBench modeling tool under User Code Definition - LossReason.

Property.Name: RecordAllQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Used to indicate whether or not entire quantity of the container will be lost for the specific container. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the entire quantity of the container will be lost. A "false" value requires the user to input the quantity of material to be lost.

Property.Name: TypeSortOrder
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The field is used to specify sort order for the result returned from the ChangeQtyTypes query. The Default Values are: 10 = Loss 20 = Bonus 30 = Sell 40 = Buy 50 = Adjust

The list of attributes and values that will override the values copied to the new container from the FromContainer.

Property.Name: ChildContainers

Property.Name: Qty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The amount of material to be split into the ToContainer

Property.Name: Qty2
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The amount of material to be split into the ToContainer using a different unit of measure than the Qty Field.

Property.Name: ToContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is a hidden reference to the new container. It will be used to map to the history.

Property.Name: ToContainerName
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The name of the container to hold the split off containers/material.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Containers to be moved from FromContainer to Svc.Container as part of this transaction

Property.Name: CloseWhenEmpty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: This is used to specify whether or not a container will be closed if a container quantity reaches zero. A "true" value (checked) indicates that the status of the container will be set to 2 (= closed) following the Combine transaction.

Property.Name: CombineAllQty
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: A flag that indicates that all available Qty and Qty2 or all child containers will be moved from the FromContainer to the ToContainer.

Property.Name: FromContainer
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: The Container against which the service is being performed. A container is a tracking mechanism used for WIP material processed in the factory.

Property.Name: ChildContainerLevel
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.

Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Unique name for this instance

Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: ChargeToStep
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Resource
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

Property.Name: ResourceStatusCode
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

Property.Name: Employee
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.

Property.Name: Product
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

Property.Name: RCount
Property.customAttribute:Annotations: Record Count

Property.Name: Step
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.

Property.Name: Workflow
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.

Property.Name: User
Property.customAttribute:Annotations:
An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.
